title: Tormach lathe G76 (inch): floored J makes LinuxCNC cut ceil(K/J) = 4 passes where the record verified 3

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` (`g76Grid`) takes J (first depth) to the grid with `floor` and K from the rounded peak and outward-rounded root, each on its own. LinuxCNC's `R1` (constant depth) ladder cuts J, 2J, ... clamped at K, so it cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The inch golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc` posts `G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0`: 0.0944 / 0.0314 = 3.006, so the control cuts 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942 and a 0.0944 pass (0.0002 in on diameter), 4 passes where the record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius). The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is exact.

Not a gouge: the extra pass is shallower than the root and the root is rounded outward. But the posted words state a pass schedule that was not verified, the same class of mismatch #417 removes on the Fanuc lathe (PR #517 review, where the Fanuc inch R was fixed by deriving it from the rounded words' own ladder).

Expected: the grid words' own ladder cuts exactly the record's pass count: e.g. choose J (and K within the outward-root rule) so ceil(K/J) equals the record's rung count, or refuse by name when the grid cannot state it. Semantics from the LinuxCNC G76 documentation (R1 = constant depth, K = full depth).

Note: the inch golden was run on the PathPilot Hub 8L sim to M30 with no alarm (PR #517 comments); that run does not check the pass count. A fix changes that golden and needs a new Hub run.

Found while fixing the M3 review of PR #517 (#417); left out of that PR because its Tormach goldens must stay byte-identical to main.

Done means: the Tormach inch G76 words make LinuxCNC's ladder cut exactly the record's passes (a test parses the posted J/K and counts ceil(K/J) against the record), or the record is refused by name; mm output unchanged.
